canonical_statement: On every nonempty open real interval, differentiable prescribed curvature kappa > 0 and differentiable prescribed signed torsion are realized by a C3 unit-speed curve in oriented Euclidean three-space, and any two realizing curves agree on the interval after an orientation-preserving Euclidean rigid motion.
domain_and_universes: a b : Real with a < b; kappa tau : Real -> Real; curves Real -> (Fin 3 -> Real); Prop in Lean universe 0
ordered_binders: forall s in Ioo a b, 0 < kappa s
conclusion: A C3 unit-speed realizing curve exists; every two realizing curves differ on Ioo a b by a dot-product-preserving linear equivalence of determinant one followed by translation.
encoding_notes: E3 is Fin 3 -> Real. An explicit dot product and square-root length avoid the Pi supremum norm. Curvature is length of the second within-derivative; signed torsion is dot(c' cross c'', c''') divided by the squared cross-product length. All derivative and congruence requirements are restricted to the open interval.
source_alignment: The statement selects the differentiable-coefficient, C3-curve, open-interval version reported for do Carmo's fundamental theorem candidate. Exact edition/page inspection remains an H-gate task and is not claimed by this statement receipt.

killed: changing coefficient hypotheses from the open to the closed interval

degenerate_cases: a < b excludes empty and singleton parameter intervals. Zero curvature is excluded pointwise; zero torsion is allowed. The target fixes parameter orientation and signed torsion and therefore only permits determinant-one rigid motions.
status_boundary: Statement-only evidence: no anchor-audit, proof, kernel closure of the theorem, or release credit is claimed.
